subject: Renewal: proposed term-swap + SLA top-up + one-time credit
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Rogers <emma@elara.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion follow-up — commercial asks and timeline

Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Elara's usage profile is shifting considerably into Q4 (expected +45% token consumption on our hosted endpoints), and procurement asked us to put the renewal offer in writing so they can sign off before their board on 10/14.

Quick summary of what Elara requested and what I'd like to take to the execs for approval:
- One-time usage credit: $50,000 to cover the projected spike during onboarding of new models.
- Term swap/reset: move 6 months of the current 12-month invoice schedule so their finance team can align renewal to calendar year (effectively a 6-month term reset).
- Pricing concession: 20% off list for year 1 of the renewed agreement (they cite competing vendor leverage).
- SLA top-up: add a 99.95% SLO for second-line support hours (12 additional SLO hours / year) and a defined makegood credit tied to incident duration.

Why this matters: Elara is a product-led fintech that is strategically important (piloting our batch embeddings + streaming for risk models). If we lose them they will likely move to an alternate provider with better near-term economics. My ask: can we get an internal OK to offer the combination above (or a narrowed variant) so I can return with final language for procurement? Procurement deadline: they want a signed order form by 2026-10-07 to meet their internal close window.

Attachments: renewal_summary.xlsx (usage forecast, margin impact), SLA_addendum_draft.pdf (initial wording).

Thanks — I'll pull margin numbers if helpful.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Naomi / Emma — reading through the ask. High level: I support doing what we can to retain Elara, but we need to be explicit on upside and downside for Redwood. A few questions and a counter-proposal: 

1) $50k credit is materially large relative to the expected margin on the next 12 months. Can we consider a usage-credit tied to milestones (e.g., onboarding complete + 30 days) rather than an unconditional credit?
2) Instead of a straight 20% first-year discount, suggest a stepped discount: 10% year 1 + 5% year 2 performance unlock tied to ARR growth through our API. Keeps runway for us while giving them short-term relief.
3) For the term swap: rather than a 6-month reset, what about converting 3 months of invoices into a prepaid credit on their account (term-swap with prepay) — keeps accounting cleaner.
4) SLA top-up: agree to add the 12 SLO hours as a one-time concession but require a signed SLA addendum and legal approval for the makegood language.

If we proceed with a mitigated package (10%+performance unlock, $30k conditional credit, 3-month prepay swap, SLA addendum), I think we can make the economics work. Naomi — can you quantify the ARR risk if we don't concede at least some of this? If risk looks high, I'll escalate to Stephanie for one-time authority.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Renewals

Marcus — appreciate the quick feedback. Short answers and added context for the exec packet: 

- ARR risk: If we do not offer a competitive near-term credit/discount, Elara's procurement team indicates they will re-run an RFP and prioritize vendors with immediate price relief. Probability of churn within 90 days is ~60% (they have two PoCs already with competitors). Current 12-month committed ARR: $620,000. Losing them or a partial downgrade would represent an expected ARR loss of $300–420k over the next 12 months.

- Conditional credit approach: I can accept $30k tied to onboarding milestone + 60 days usage threshold. That is acceptable to them but they'll push for unconditional.

- Term mechanics: Elara's accounting team says a 6-month alignment is their hard requirement; they cannot take vendor invoices that bridge fiscal periods. They asked specifically for a 6-month reset rather than a prepay. I'll attach their procurement note (redwood_pricing_model.csv contains their payment schedule). If we can't do the full reset, they'll ask to re-evaluate vendor options.

- SLA wording: procurement will not sign anything without concrete makegood language. Draft attached.

Links:

Team — thanks for the clear thread and the commercial rationale. Given the ARR at risk and the strategic nature of Elara's workload, I approve a one-time concession package with these firm limits and gating controls: 

- Pricing discount: up to 15% off list for the first 12 months (not to exceed) with a 3% performance-based credit in year 2 tied to API adoption metrics;
- One-time usage credit: up to $30,000, conditional on onboarding milestones (as Naomi suggested) and payable only after milestone verification;
- Term alignment: authorize up to a 4-month term reset (not the full 6 months requested) — finance must confirm revenue recognition impact;
- SLA top-up: approve the 12 additional SLO hours and inclusion of a makegood credit; Legal to finalize SLA addendum language and sign;

Conditions: Legal MUST sign the SLA addendum; Finance sign-off on revenue recognition for the term-reset; Product to confirm there's no operational risk in granting the SLA hours. If any of the gating reviews fail, the concessions are void.

Naomi — please prepare a concise final order form with the negotiated terms (reflecting the above limits) and run it through Legal/Finance. Copy me and Neha on the final DocuSign packet. If Elara will not accept the 4-month swap and insists on 6 months plus an unconditional $50k credit, escalate back to me immediately and include the exact tradeoffs they demand.

Thanks — Stephanie
